OPDI Sensors

Sensors Deployed

12

Airports Covered

7

Countries

4

Observed flight hours/day

~2,370

Overview

The OPDI Sensors is an initiative to extend the OpenSky Network crowd-sourced receiver network by deploying ground-based ADS-B sensors at strategic airport locations. The aim is to improve ground-based and low-altitude ADS-B coverage around airports, especially where existing coverage in the OpenSky Network is limited.

In collaboration with the Performance Review Commission, each deployed sensor receives ADS-B transponder signals from aircraft in its vicinity, providing position, altitude, speed, and identification data. The collected data feeds into the OpenSky Network and is subsequently used by the OPDI, enabling performance monitoring at airports that were previously unobservable through open data sources.

This page describes the network as it stands: where the receivers are, whether they are reporting, and how far each one sees. Two companion pages take the argument further — Impact on Airport Monitoring measures what the sensors added, and Where Next identifies the airports that remain unobserved.

Sensor Coverage

Each Open Performance Data Initiative (OPDI) sensor’s reception footprint, as measured by the OpenSky Network (OSN): the polygon traces the furthest aircraft position received in each compass direction. Zoom in to inspect an individual airport; hover a sensor for its serial and maximum range.

Coverage measured 2026-07-10. 1 of 12 sensors reported no coverage in the sampled period.

The map shows what each receiver reaches. Whether that reach added anything — aircraft nobody else was seeing — is a separate question, answered under Impact on Airport Monitoring.
